EMG signalsEach EMG signal is one channel of the loaded Poly5 file, labelled with the muscle it records from. All signals share one time axis, so they line up below each other.Channel 1 (EMGdi) is the diaphragm signal. emg.preprocess and emg.ecg_gating use it by default. The raw signals still contain the ECG; emg.ecg_gating removes it before emg.detect_breaths runs.

Files Drag on a file to select a section.Drag a section to slide it, or drag its edge to change its length. The arrow keys move a selected section by 0.1 s (with Shift: 1.0 s). The × removes it.Merge order sets the order of the sections. Merge sections joins them into one recording.
Channels Tick a channel to show it on the file lanes and in the plots below.Esophageal, gastric and transpulmonary pressure are also known categories. Tick them to show the extra signals of a recording with an esophageal pressure (P_es) catheter.

—
Ventilator signalsThe channel numbers come from ventilator.channels (pressure_channel, flow_channel, volume_channel). Each signal is labelled with its category from m3resp.data.categories.

Raw synchronizationThe ventilator is the reference. The offset of a recording, in seconds, is where its first sample sits on the ventilator time line. The bar of each row shows it.Signal is the signal of the row; Compared with is the ventilator signal it is matched to. EMG signals are compared as their envelope (RMS over 0.3 s, ECG removed).An empty offset field uses the estimated offset: the cross-correlation of the two signals, over −5.0 to +5.0 s. A change of signal gives a new estimate.Type a value to replace the estimate. With the method estimate_offset, Estimate finds the offsets of all rows again and clears the typed values.Match is the correlation at the offset in use (1 is the same shape).session.sync_raw applies the offsets.

Working windowCut out the part of the recording that 2 · Design analyses.Each lane is an overview (minimum and maximum) of the signal in the section of that modality. The ventilator lanes follow the channels ticked there.Keep window adds a span to keep. Drag its band to move it, or a handle to change its length. Click a window, on the lanes or in the list, to edit it with the Start and End fields.Remove window adds a span to cut out (hatched red). Everything around it is kept. Use it to remove a cough or a disconnection from the middle of a recording.Whole signal makes one keep window over the whole recording and joins the other keep windows into it. On its own it saves the recording unchanged. With remove windows, it keeps everything except those spans.With only remove windows, the whole recording minus those spans is saved.The keep/remove chip of a row changes it between the two.Save as new sequence joins the segments, in time order, into one named sequence (eit.slice followed by Sequence.concatenate()). It adds the sequence to Saved sequences, under this card and in the side panel. The saved windows turn grey and are locked. New windows make the next sequence. Remove a sequence to unlock its windows.
